comments.author: robogame_dev
comments.body: OpenAI and Anthropic models are tuned to "outsmart" the user and do a lot more than you asked for or do it differently. If you know you want it to do a task a certain way, and not discover it's own path, you want a less opinionated model that is happy to execute without adding it's own design input on top. I usually main GLM because it's instruction following is excellent, always coloring inside the lines so to speak.

replies.author: AssiduousLayabout

replies.author: robogame_dev
replies.body:
https://i.redd.it/asy11vodk2zh1.png

No kidding - Qwen's intelligence to time ratio is abysmal - it basically goes in circles until it eventually makes it. I have all the major AI subs and my qwen sub is the worst cost-to-results ratio. replies.author: thatguywithimpact
replies.body:
I lot of is just because being very new to agentic AI gamedev, I find myself constantly limit testing models to try to see what they can and can't do. It keeps surprising me, but I also developed a much better sense on how to utilize it better.

I remember making blender plug in a few years back with old rudimentary AI(non agent ) and it made incredibly efficient algorithm far faster than I expected and just blew way past my expectations. But then for easy part which is plug-in UI with literally 5 buttons it just couldn't do anything. I ended up writing UI myself.


And with modern AI it's the same thing, it keeps being this incredibly genius Savant that can't tie it's own shoe laces.  And there's a huge difference between right prompt and wrong prompt

replies.author: Adevyy
replies.body:
I don’t experience this with Claude. In fact, I often get a simple outcome from it, realise that it being engineered harder would fit it better, and then ask for improvements because of that.

The only "outsmarting" Opus 5.5 seems to provide me with suggestions and they are often surprisingly helpful because it seems to consider the reasoning behind my request.

If a Claude model seems to often "outsmart" you to the point of it being annoying, I'd think that your promoting can be improved.
